events.title: Local consumer groups ask media to explain why above-target inflation still matters for households
events.expected_impact: Slightly raises salience of inflation-risk arguments among the broader public and may nudge media framing toward caution rather than pure cut anticipation.

events.title: Local labor-worry stories enter consumer coverage
events.expected_impact: Slightly raises attention to the employment side of the Fed tradeoff and gives doves more visible public context, while not overwhelming inflation concerns.

events.title: Street pricing note shifts toward two-way December scenario bands
events.expected_impact: Raises market attention, dampens one-way conviction, and increases incremental repricing off labor and inflation signals.

events.title: Request for updated pre-meeting staff briefing
events.expected_impact: Reinforces data dependence, sharpens internal comparison of cut versus hold, and may reduce public over-interpretation of technical adjustments.

events.title: Request for tighter public messaging discipline before meeting
events.expected_impact: Reduces market overconfidence in easing, limits narrative drift, and helps maintain committee flexibility.

events.title: Dovish camp circulates conditional labor-risk briefing
events.expected_impact: Slightly raises salience of labor-softening risks for centrists without forcing a public split; preserves data-dependent framing and keeps a 25bp discussion live rather than larger-move speculation.

events.title: Chair reiterates data-dependent framework in public remarks
events.expected_impact: Reduces overinterpretation of easing odds, preserves optionality, and supports committee cohesion across hawkish and dovish camps.

events.title: Internal committee briefing focused on dual-risk assessment
events.expected_impact: Improves consensus management and keeps both cut and hold pathways procedurally legitimate pending data.

simulation_brief.summary: Late-2025 FOMC decision environment with markets discussing a possible quarter-point cut amid mixed labor-market softening and inflation still above target. Policymakers emphasize data dependence rather than pre-commitment. Terminal question is whether the target range for the federal funds rate is lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 meeting statement than immediately before the meeting.
simulation_brief.resolution_rule: yes only if target range is lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 statement than immediately before the meeting; implementation-detail changes alone do not count.
simulation_brief.initial_state_uncertainty: High uncertainty around whether labor softening or inflation persistence dominates the committee decision. Source corpus is sparse and defines endpoint tightly.

important_questions: Will the FOMC lower the target range for the federal funds rate at the December 10, 2025 meeting relative to immediately before the meeting?
By the eve of the meeting, do incoming data appear to shift the effective internal balance toward hawks, doves, or leave centrists dominant?
Before the meeting, does market and analyst consensus move toward treating a 25bp cut as the base case or remain split/lean hold?
At decision time, is there any technical or implementation change that creates headline confusion without satisfying the target-range-lowered criterion?
